test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a swimming pool measuring 90 m × 40 m, 150 men take a dip. If the average displacement of water by a man is 8 m³, then what will be the rise in the water level of the pool?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rise in water level = (**Total Volume Displaced**) ÷ (**Area of Pool Base**)

Total displacement = 150 men × 8 m³ = 1200 m³

Area of pool = 90 m × 40 m = 3600 m²

Rise (h) = 1200 ÷ 3600 = 1/3 m

Rise in cm = (1/3) × 100 = 33.33 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dimensions of **swimming pool** = 90 m × 40 m

Number of **men** = 150

Average **displacement** per man = 8 m³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of water rose = Total volume displaced by men

Area of base × **Rise in height (h)** = Number of men × Volume displaced per man

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0af9afdb7d2882419098ae00ee3cc0930523eee39286844bd3ff082c5ae3ef63.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total volume of water displaced = 150 × 8 = 1200 m³

⇒ Surface area of the pool = 90 × 40 = 3600 m²

⇒ Let **h** be the rise in water level in meters.

⇒ 3600 × h = 1200

⇒ h = 1200 ÷ 3600

⇒ h = 1/3 m

⇒ To convert meters into **centimeters**, multiply by 100:

⇒ h = (1/3) × 100 cm

⇒ h ≈ 33.33 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Archimedes' Principle

The volume of water displaced by a submerged or floating object is exactly equal to the volume of the object itself.

Volume of a Cuboid

The volume of a cuboidal pool is calculated as V = Length × Width × Depth (or height).

Rise in Level Formula

Rise in Level = (Volume Added) ÷ (Area of the Base). This assumes the base area remains constant throughout the rise.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert meters to centimeters, multiply by 100; to convert cubic meters to liters, multiply by 1000.</p
